title: Test-Time Search & Selection
description: Study candidate generation and diversity, self-consistency and its limits, search budgets and stopping, and ranking and best-of-n selection. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Candidate generation and diversity
lessons.description: Define a candidate set with distinct methods and a shared verification rule.
lessons.conceptOverview: Generating multiple candidates can explore alternatives, but correlated candidates may repeat the same mistake. Diversity should concern solution strategies or evidence, not merely wording.

lessons.title: Self-consistency and its limits
lessons.description: Identify the shared assumption before accepting the majority.
lessons.conceptOverview: Agreement among sampled answers can improve selection on some tasks but does not prove truth. Correlated errors and ambiguous questions can produce a strong majority for an incorrect answer.
lessons.whyItMatters: Consensus should be checked against task evidence and assumptions.

lessons.title: Search budgets and stopping
lessons.description: Define success, exhaustion and escalation conditions.
lessons.conceptOverview: Allocate computation based on task difficulty, uncertainty and verifier feedback. Stop when the acceptance criterion is met or the budget is exhausted, and report unresolved cases honestly.

lessons.title: Ranking and best-of-N selection
lessons.description: Design a correctness-focused check separate from the ranking score.
lessons.conceptOverview: Best-of-N selects candidates using a score or verifier. Selection can exploit weaknesses in the scoring function, so evaluate chosen outputs rather than assuming higher scores mean higher true quality.
lessons.whyItMatters: Selection quality depends on the scoring function's validity.
